# Fixture 0077 — access-log `response_flag_filter` (`flags: [NR]`, byte-exact)

The **SECOND access-log FILTER witness** (phase 71, ADR-0144 / ADR-0145),
sibling to fixture 0076 (`status_code_filter`). It witnesses the second
`AccessLogFilter` oneof arm: an `AccessLog` entry carrying
`filter.response_flag_filter.flags: [NR]` emits a record only when its single
`%RESPONSE_FLAGS%` token is one of `flags`.

## What this proves (the filter decision is cross-proxy identical on BOTH halves)

One HCM listener, one file sink, one `direct_response` route, probed with two
requests:

| # | request        | response | `%RESPONSE_FLAGS%` | in `[NR]`? | emitted? |
|---|----------------|----------|--------------------|------------|----------|
| 1 | `GET /direct`  | 503      | `-` (direct auth.) | no         | NO       |
| 2 | `GET /nowhere` | 404      | `NR` (no route)    | yes        | YES      |

So each proxy's file holds EXACTLY ONE line (measured against the pinned
`envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`, ADR-0145 PV-6 live measurement):

```
STATUS=404 PATH=/nowhere FLAGS=NR
```

Both halves are load-bearing. The KEPT half proves the filter does not suppress
a matching `NR` record; the DROPPED half proves it suppresses a non-matching
`-` record. A one-sided disagreement — either proxy emitting a `/direct` line,
or either proxy dropping the `/nowhere` line — fails the driver's line-count
assertion before the byte compare is even reached.

`%RESPONSE_FLAGS%` renders `-` on the 503: a `direct_response` is generated by
the HCM itself, so no upstream failure flag applies, and `-` is ∉ the 29-token
response-flag set, so it never matches a non-empty `flags`. The 404 renders
`NR` (NoRouteFound) because `/nowhere` matches no route — the deterministic
no-route path that fixtures 0056-family (`access_log_rf_no_route`) already
witness.

The assertion is **pure cross-proxy equality** — there is NO static expected
literal. The line above is documentation of the measured value, not the oracle.

## Ordering witness (CF-70-3)

The dropped probe (`/direct`) is FIRST and the kept probe (`/nowhere`) is LAST.
This kept-last ordering is the sound convention (FileAccessLog flushes in
request order, so once the kept `/nowhere` line is on disk — which the driver's
`wait_file_lines(1)` waits for — every earlier non-suppressed record has also
flushed), but it is NOT enforced: ADR-0146 RETIRED the hard "last probe must be
kept" assertion because it is incompatible with the pre-existing dropped-last
fixture 0076. The CF-70-3 closure is the driver's bounded settle (both proxies
still live, re-read both files after a fixed wait, reject any growth past the
kept-line count) — ordering-agnostic, so it protects both 0076 and 0077. This is
the fixture that first exercises that path (`has_suppression == true`).

## Probes / driver

`kind: http1_access_log_byte_exact` — drives the probe sequence, scrapes both
files, asserts the scraped line count equals `expected_logged_count(probes)`
(= 1 here, the lone kept probe), and calls
`access_log::assert_access_log_lines_byte_identical`. Probe 1 carries
`expect_logged: false`, excluding it from that count.

`clusters: []` — the only route is `direct_response` and `/nowhere` is a
no-route synth, so there is no upstream: no backend spawns and no
`{{BACKEND_IP}}` machinery is needed.

## Per-side divergences

| Side       | bind address | admin block  | access-log path                         | `generate_request_id`   |
|------------|--------------|--------------|-----------------------------------------|-------------------------|
| envoy      | `0.0.0.0`    | yes (port 0) | `/tmp/0077-envoy-mount/access.log`      | `false` (load-bearing)  |
| envoy-rust | `127.0.0.1`  | omitted      | `/tmp/0077-envoy-rust-mount/access.log` | omitted (never injects) |

The route table, the `text_format_source`, and the `filter` block are
BYTE-IDENTICAL across the two files — only the four documented per-side deltas
above differ, exactly as in fixtures 0040 / 0056 / 0076.
